audit.whatIsWrong: Verdict correct and both layers already agree; the difficulty was never grounded.
audit.why: 55.79% over 1649 games, FAVOURED 4/10. Packet levelChart, content win[0..6] and full phases[].side all read Fizz on all seven rows — no cross-layer disagreement. Swain has no dash in his kit; his only lockdown is Nevermove at 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s and 850 range, and Demonic Ascension is a flat 120s.
audit.corrected: Chart untouched. Difficulty grounded in the missing dash and the Nevermove return mechanic.

audit.whatIsWrong: Demonic Ascension was described only as 'sustain', with no cooldown and no mention that it shortens Nevermove.
audit.why: Riot's text: Demonic Ascension is a flat 120s at every rank, drains from a 650 radius, and stays active indefinitely while he is draining champions. Riot's Nevermove text adds 'This ability has a shorter cooldown during Demonic Ascension' — so the root you dodged once comes back faster once his ultimate is up. That is a real spike change the page never recorded.
audit.corrected: Written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, winCon and the content mid paragraph.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never said that Nevermove roots on its RETURN pass, and repeatedly called it 'short range'.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits. Swain can then choose to pull all rooted champions closer.' The outgoing wave does not root — the return does, and the pull follows. It is also 850 range, which is longer than anything Fizz has. The page described it as short-range and easy to bait, which teaches the reader to dodge the wrong half of the ability.
audit.corrected: Corrected in tldr, loading, phases[2].why, phases[3].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[0].d, whys[0], wants.you[0], spikes[0].text and the early paragraph.

notes:
FABRICATED ABILITY NAME the packet missed: wants.foe[1] said 'Land Torment (E) to root you'. Torment is not a Swain ability — his E is Nevermove. The packet's suspectNames only flagged two harmless near-misses on 'Demonic Ascension' and did not catch this one.

BIGGEST MECHANICAL FIX: Nevermove roots on the RETURN pass, not the outgoing one, and it is 850 range. The page called it 'short range and easy to bait out' in three separate fields, which teaches the reader to dodge the half of the ability that does nothing. Riot's text is explicit: the wave 'then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits', after which he can pull rooted champions closer.

SECOND MECHANICAL FIX: Riot's Nevermove text also says the ability has a shorter cooldown during Demonic Ascension — so the root gets faster inside his ultimate. That interaction appeared nowhere on the page.

ANTI-HEAL: both missingInteractions rules apply and are supported by the kit flags (Ravenous Flock carries heal and percentHealth). Grievous Wounds timing is now stated in four fields instead of a single passing mention in a report entry.

ALSO FIXED: wants.you[2] said to all-in 'after his Ravenous Flock stacks reset (post-recast)'. Ravenous Flock is a passive with no cast and no recast, so that instruction described a window that does not exist.

CHART: no edits — packet levelChart, content win[0..6] and full phases[].side all read Fizz on all seven rows.

UNVERIFIED, not written: whether Playful/Trickster's untargetability breaks an already-applied Nevermove root or only avoids the return pass, and whether Chum the Waters' knockup can displace Swain out of his own Demonic Ascension drain radius.
